thread:
amelia: flagged — multiple customers reporting 504s + timeouts to /v1/generate since ~08:42 UTC. Seeing spike in p95. anybody oncall can confirm? :eyes:
sre-oncall: I see the spike in hosted-eu and hosted-us-east. Errors are 504 gateway timeouts from inference-gateway. Rolling traces now.
sam: grabbing traces — initial looks like requests reached auth-proxy but stalled on POST /infer upstream for ~30s, then gateway timed out.
marta: customer support forwarded a curl repro. Posting here: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"rwd-xl","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate``` Response sometimes 504, sometimes eventually 200 after 37s.
vincent: adding tracing spans — auth-proxy -> runtime-front -> model-worker. The majority of latency is auth-proxy waiting on kv-cache GET (auth-session) which sometimes takes 10-20s.
ops-bot: deploy detected: canary rollout rwd-xl@2026-03-17T08:30 by deploy-bot (10% canary).
amelia: hmm canary started ~08:30, first errors ~08:42. correlation looks strong. Can we pause canary?
deploy-bot: canary paused by sam at 08:46 UTC.
lucas: quick check of auth-kv: noticed increased tail latency on redis cluster shard 3, CPU spiking and a handful of slow commands. Possible eviction/GC?
qa-bot: I replayed a batch of synthetic requests against canary instances — saw auth GET latency >15s occasionally, causing gateway to hit 30s timeout.
sam: mitigation steps: 1) pause canary (done), 2) enable fallback routing for affected routes to rwd-small, 3) temporary increase gateway timeout to 60s for in-flight canary traffic while we investigate — any objections?
marta: fallback routing done at 08:49 for /v1/generate to rwd-small for requests hitting high latency. Customer impact down but some requests served by smaller model -> quality drop.
vincent: investigating redis — there are ~3 large scan jobs from analytics hitting the same shard during canary warmup. Kicking off rate-limit on those jobs now.
sre-oncall: action: roll forward or rollback? pause is fine. I'd prefer rollback to stable if root cause not identified by 09:15.
amelia: agree. also add an alert for redis slow-command > 500ms on any shard.
lucas: root cause draft: canary introduced increased auth-check rate (different header flow) which amplified existing background scan on shard 3 causing slow commands -> auth-proxy stalls -> gateway 504s.
sam: logs attached (snippet): ```[08:44:12] auth-proxy GET kv auth:session:abc123 latency=16321ms shard=3
[08:44:13] runtime-front request_id=xyz status=504 upstream_wait=30000ms```
vincent: immediate fixes: 1) throttle background scan, 2) promote redis failover for shard 3 (in progress), 3) add circuit-breaker in auth-proxy to fallback to token-check service to avoid 20s stalls.
amelia: owners: Lucas = root-cause + postmortem, Sam = rollback + canary gating checklist, Marta = customer comms + support ticket linking.
sre-oncall: creating incident ticket INC-4567 and assigning owners. Will run postmortem template.
ops-bot: INC-4567 created by sre-oncall. Priority P1 -> P2 after fallback enabled.
lucas: postmortem items (quick list): - root cause writeup - canary preflight checklist (redis hotspot detection) - auth-proxy circuit-breaker implementation - redis slow-command alerts and autoscaling - add canary abort if kv latency > 500ms threshold - customer comms template - SLO review for gateway timeouts
amelia: timeline for fixes? suggest hotfix for circuit-breaker + redis throttle today; canary gating changes next sprint.
sam: rolling back canary artifact to stable at 08:58 UTC. Monitoring.
qa-bot: after rollback and throttles, p95 back to normal by 09:03. No further 504s reported.
marta: sending update to affected customers and linking INC-4567, noting temporary fallback to smaller model and expected quality delta.
lucas: I'll own the postmortem and post initial draft by EOD. Tagging follow-ups for next retro.
sre-oncall: thanks all — closing warroom but keeping ticket open for postmortem action items. :white_check_mark:
